headline: High risk: dexter’s broad networked autonomous execution can leak financial data and amplify unsafe downstream actions when paired with ai-engineering-hub’s MCP/RAG-oriented content handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is tagged with MCP/RAG and may ingest external content, while dexter runs autonomously and can consume outputs from other tools. No shared channel is documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the pair is connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge
IF dexter parses ai-engineering-hub output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or workspace between the agents
Require provenance labels on all inter-agent messages
Insert a human review step before dexter executes instructions
Restrict ai-engineering-hub to read-only outputs
requires-engineering: add channel-level provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data, uses multiple external APIs, and requests many secrets; ai-engineering-hub has broad network egress listed as none, but if it receives dexter outputs or shared files, sensitive data can still be exposed through dexter’s outbound API calls. The default networked, secret-bearing setup makes leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents share any workspace containing financial data
IF dexter forwards shared file contents to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or Financial Datasets APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove unused API keys from dexter’s environment
Block outbound calls except allowlisted endpoints
Store sensitive files outside .dexter/scratchpad/
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, so concurrent writes can conflict if ai-engineering-hub also writes into the same directory or shared repo. The profiles do not prove a shared writable path, so this is an inferred overlap rather than a documented collision.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same checkout or scratch directory
IF ai-engineering-hub writes files while dexter runs multiple instances
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Run only one dexter instance per workspace
Make shared paths read-only
Use file locks around scratchpad writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is designed for autonomous execution, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub output as guidance, it may act without verification. ai-engineering-hub’s MCP/RAG-oriented content can be treated as authoritative by downstream automation, creating a direct path from generated content to external actions.
conditions: IF dexter uses ai-engineering-hub output as an execution plan
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted before dexter acts
mitigations: Require explicit validation before execution
Limit dexter to draft-only mode
Add a second model to cross-check outputs
Log and review all autonomous actions
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: dexter processes financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while ai-engineering-hub has no documented compliance controls or residency guarantees. If regulated financial data or EU PII enters the pair, the lack of documented residency and retention controls creates a plausible compliance breach; uncertainty warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through dexter’s external APIs
IF any EU personal data is stored or logged without a documented DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of dexter inputs
Review API vendor DPAs and residency settings
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Document retention and deletion procedures
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
